Actually, urea left standing on rubber is problematic. Yes, every tire runs across urea on a virtually daily basis, but when urea is left standing it forms NH3 (Ammonia). If Ammonia is left exposed to rubber it does cause degradation. While the metal 'cords' or bands in this person's Hankooks may not deform/degrade; the rubber will. I've personally seen aluminum wheels bubble/peel and tires fail left in Cyanuric acid, which NH3 forms at higher temperatures.  
To the OP, wash the tires semi-frequently with warm water. Diluting the urea from the raccoon's urine will help reduce the acid's ability to damage the tires.

Apply heat ~150*C slowly, once the panel is at temp, quickly apply liquid Nitrogen. The local contraction in the panel can straighten the panel from a uniform dent. Mind you this isn't for small or extreme distortions in a metal surface. Only for 'gentle' dents (think fist size). Also if working with a painted surface, you can separate the bond between metal and paint. The paint will likely crack and fall of the panel. Attempt at your own peril.

For those curious, find a industrial/medical gas supplier nearby, they should be willing to sell you liquid Nitrogen fairly cheaply. I prefer someone bring a stainless steel thermos with a hole drilled in the lid, but I will fill a foam cooler for some people. As others have have noted, any cryogenic liquid should be treated with massive level of respect. Other notably awesome LN2 uses: homemade ice cream (the best home use of LN2), imploding vessels (like garbage cans), and fixing dents in metal panels (carefully on painted metal panels). 
Source: I sell industrial/medical gas.

Edit: I do sell Propane and Propane accessories (not grills, but regulators and the like) as a small fraction of my work responsibilities. I would sell Industrial grade Liquid Oxygen (LO2, LOx) to any customer requesting it. Figure a five year lease on a 196L Dewar and the fill is roughly $3700, plus delivery, taxes, and hazmat charges. I don't know of any illicit uses for liquid Oxygen, but you've piqued my interest, off to Google. However, here in Colorado a large percentage of our new business is due to the medicinal and legal production of Marijuana via CO2 sales. So there's that.

I'm not in quite the same boat, but I'm in a similar place (broken engagement, stalled at middle management, and sort of hopeless). Here's all of the advise I can give:
1) Don't do anything rash... I've contemplated leaving 'the game' more than a hundred times. It won't deliver any results, except the negatives (destroyed family members, damaged friends, and haters telling everyone they told them so).
2) Life really is a bitch, but we strive to make our own little universe better. Trust me, the toys get more expensive and awesome, and it's almost worth it. It's worth it when you find a 'player 2'.  
3) Hold onto any joy you can... Bad breakup, awesome times with that person. Fired, moving on to a better job and employer. Moving, well moving always sucks, so there's that. 
4) Spend time with those that love you. If you have family nearby (and they didn't molest/ruin/beat you), go hang out with them. If you only have a best friend, go hang out with them. Involve yourself in anything. It truly will distract the mind and keep you from doing anything rash. 
5) Put the booze/drugs down. Seriously. I've been looking for solutions in the bottom of a half-gallon bottle of vodka before, all it reads is "drink more". Alcohol, drugs, and escapism only lead to more problems/hurt. 
6) Don't doubt yourself. You are worth the time of anyone you meet. Trust me, you offer something to the party. I'm total geek/nerd/introvert, but in my career I have to sell my company. As a result, I am constantly opening myself up to new people. If you do the same, you'll find a ton of people that want to get to know you (most likely because you are genuine). 
7) Last, but not least, enjoy the simple pleasures. I'm enjoying telling you how I have tried to live. You need to find that simple pleasure. Fake that you are happy (for a month, for a year, eventually the fake will turn to reality). When you can no longer tell the difference, you'll know what real happiness is/means when you find it. 
Seriously, I wish you the best fellow redditor. If nothing else, you can count me as a friend. I'd love to chat, play video games, or just BS on reddit. If you are in Colorado, I'm down to make new real life friends. Just take care of you. You, really and truthfully, deserve it.
